Tomas Skrivan said:

(it is all using FloatArray I didn't bother with Array Float as I just assumed it would be terrible but maybe it I should include it :)

Henrik Böving said:

Array Float would be equivalent to a double** in C

Is there any plan to in future have Array Float compile to a double*, which is what I assume docs#FloatArray does? What about Array (Prod Float Float) compiling to a contiguous array of struct {double; double} *?

I would say there is a desire to do so but much less of a plan :D. One of the crucial questions is of course, what happens when an Array Float, represented as a double* crosses an FFI boundary to a function that wants an Array a where a is abstract. Currently for unboxed types our reaction would be box it! But that would mean reallocating a double** array. We could work around this to a limited capacity by somehow marking the array as such in the runtime and taking some branches in array operations but that would slow down all ordinary array ops at the cost of Float so this is not a clear win in my opinion. In addition this approach makes special casing Array (Float x Float) hard. The big issue here is that Lean is not fully monomorphized so these tricks always have to consider what happens at boundaries.

In the library I'm working on, a tensor/array of Prod Float Float is still just FloatArray with appropriately adjusted indexing.

There is a class that provides an interface on how to read and write a type to contiguous memory. So you can take arbitrary products. Make structures and store product in them etc. and then you make an array of such type you again get just FloatArray with appropriately adjusted indexing.

This class https://github.com/lecopivo/NumLean/blob/7f6198f2be23efbaec049a14d36b192b9ff656c3/NumLean/Interfaces/HasFlatRepr/Basic.lean#L10

For example X can be Prod Float (Prod Float Float), Ks is FloatVector(a wrapper around FloatArray guarantting size), K is Float and nX is 3.

Using this abstraction I can avoid relying on some future compiler support.

This is in essence a version of Array Float being represented as FloatArray and getting boxed when needing to be passed to a generic Array function. Though the nice advantage is that it is actually tracked at the user visible type system so the conversion is explicit rather than implicitly inserted by the compiler

As a point of reference, OCaml also has a special representation of FloatArray, but also tries to make it behave like Array Float, and there are some complications that arise from this. See e.g. https://www.lexifi.com/blog/ocaml/about-unboxed-float-arrays/ Maybe this can serve as some inspiration for what to do or what not to do.
Interesting read and he proposed pretty much the designed I ended up implementing in Lean

Yes, ocaml chooses the tagging route that I described above and pays for it with the runtime check. I know that in oxcaml you can eliminate the check with some additional modality but I think lean is not going to grow a new modality any time soon.
